neighboring_unit_entries.title: Iterated integration of the arcsine series produces log-sine moment identities
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Starting from the central-binomial expansion of arcsin(x)/x, the source integrates and differentiates to obtain related series, then constructs a polylogarithm-like hierarchy K_m(x). Repeated integration by parts and the substitution x=sin(theta/2) turn the hierarchy into integrals of powers of log(2x), hence log-sine moments.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Replacing x by ix transports the arcsine coefficient construction to an inverse-hyperbolic-sine companion, including its sign pattern. An analogous hierarchy F_m and integration by parts then convert the companion central-binomial sums into log-sinh moments.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source replaces x by ix in the preceding arcsine identities, records inverse-hyperbolic-sine series, specializes them using an inverse-hyperbolic-sine value expressed as a logarithm, and defines F_m analogously to K_m. It derives an integral representation for F_m and, after integration by parts, states a family relating alternating central-binomial sums to powers of log(2 sinh(θ/2)).
directed.conceptual_reading: The imaginary substitution constructs a hyperbolic companion without rebuilding the method from scratch. It preserves the iterative generating-function architecture while changing signs and replacing circular inverse functions by hyperbolic ones; F_m then carries the same logarithmic-degree mechanism into the new representation.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge objects are x↦ix, the inverse-hyperbolic-sine series, the logarithmic endpoint value, F_m, and integration by parts. They connect the arcsine/log-sine construction to an alternating-series/log-sinh construction.
